key_insight: Unifying known-crystal databases expands forward screening opportunities while revealing that inverse-designed materials may be less novel than claimed.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can search overlooked known crystals for target properties and assess generated candidates against a broader, structure-matched reference.
method: Match crystal structures across 55 databases, retaining source provenance.
Train CGTNet, an equivariant graph transformer, to predict missing material properties.
Compare screening and stiffness-conditioned generation at equal verification budgets.
evidence_signal: The integrated database contains 14.6 million crystals and 131.8 million property values; generation produced 100 stiff hits versus screening’s 55, but all generated hits contained osmium and 82 repeated recorded compositions.
watch_item: Only 4.5% of crystal–property pairs have recorded values, so model predictions require validation and novelty checks must go beyond composition alone.
paper_title: Probing the limits of forward screening and inverse design of crystal materials
